questions.question: A distinctive cross-shaped constellation best seen in the northern hemisphere during the summer and fall months around September is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cygnus**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cygnus** is a distinctive cross-shaped constellation best seen in the northern hemisphere during the summer and fall months around September.
 
• It is also known as the Northern Cross due to its characteristic shape.
 
• Cygnus is one of the most recognizable constellations in the night sky and is located in the Milky Way.
 
• The constellation is associated with the myth of Zeus transforming into a swan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cygnus** contains several notable stars, including Deneb, one of the brightest stars in the night sky and part of the Summer Triangle asterism.
 
• The constellation also hosts several deep-sky objects, such as the North America Nebula and the Veil Nebula.
 
• Cygnus is bordered by the constellations Draco, Lyra, Vulpecula, Pegasus, Lacerta, and Cepheus.
 
• Observation of Cygnus is best in the northern hemisphere during the late evening hours of summer and early fall.

questions.question: The point in the orbit of an object (such as a satellite) orbiting the earth that is at the greatest distance from the centre of the earth is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**apogee**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The point in the orbit of an object (such as a satellite) orbiting the earth that is at the greatest distance from the centre of the earth is known as **apogee**.
 
• Apogee is derived from the Greek words "apo," meaning away, and "ge," meaning Earth.
 
• It contrasts with **perigee**, which is the point in the orbit of an object where it is closest to the Earth.
 
• Understanding apogee and perigee is crucial for satellite operations and space missions, as it affects communication signals and orbital dynamics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aphelion** and **perihelion** are terms used to describe the farthest and nearest points of an object's orbit around the Sun, respectively.
 
• The term **perigee** is used specifically for objects orbiting the Earth, while **perihelion** is for objects orbiting the Sun.
 
• Knowledge of these orbital points is important for understanding the mechanics of celestial bodies and for planning space missions.
 
• Orbital mechanics is a fundamental aspect of astrophysics and aerospace engineering, guiding the design and operation of spacecraft. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f5219344328d7b028b2e0108b7d3f644db77d319429544bd6dd9d139def38ff4.png]

questions.question: Who calculated the approximate location of the planet Neptune by studying gravity - induced disturbances in the motion of Uranus?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Urbain-Jean-Joseph Le Verrier**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Urbain-Jean-Joseph Le Verrier** calculated the **approximate location of the planet Neptune **by studying gravity-induced disturbances in the motion of Uranus.
 
• Le Verrier's calculations were based on Newton's laws of gravitation, which predicted the presence of another planet affecting Uranus's orbit.
 
• His work led to the** discovery of Neptune on September 23, 1846, by Johann Gottfried Galle and Heinrich d'Arrest** at the **Berlin Observatory**.
 
• Le Verrier's prediction and the subsequent discovery of Neptune stand as a monumental achievement in the field of astronomy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **John Couch Adams** independently made similar calculations around the same time, but Le Verrier's work led to the actual observational discovery.
 
• Neptune is the eighth planet from the Sun and is known for its deep blue color caused by the absorption of red light by methane in its atmosphere.
 
• The discovery of Neptune was a major milestone in the validation of Newtonian mechanics.
 
• Le Verrier's methods of celestial mechanics continue to influence modern astronomy and space navigation.

questions.question: What was the name of the mega-ocean that surrounded the single continental mass before the continental drift as described by Alfred Wegener?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Panthalassa.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to Wegener, all the continents formed a single continental mass and mega ocean surrounded the same.
 
• The supercontinent was named PANGAEA, which meant all earth.
 
• The mega-ocean was called **PANTHALASSA, meaning all water.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Continental drift theory **deals with the distribution of the oceans and the continents.
 
• It was first suggested by a German meteorologist, Alfred Wegener in 1912.
 
• Around 200 million years ago Pangaea started splitting and broke down into two large continental masses as Laurasia and Gondwanaland forming the northern and southern components respectively.
 
• Subsequently, Laurasia and Gondwanaland continued to break into various smaller continents that exist today.

questions.question: Which of the following elements occurs most abundantly in our universe?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hydrogen** element occurs **most abundantly in our universe**.
 
• Hydrogen has just one proton and one electron.
 
• it's the only element without a neutron.
 
• The simplest form of the element makes it abundant in the universe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• There are only 11 elements that are gaseous.
 
• Of those 11 elements,** hydrogen and helium **make up the majority of the star, with** hydrogen at 75% and helium at 23%.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **The ten most abundant elements in the universe** in decreasing order of abundance are: 

 
• **Hydrogen**
 
• Helium
 
• **Oxygen**
 
• Carbon
 
• Neon
 
• **Nitrogen**
 
• Magnesium
 
• **Silicon**
 
• Iron
 
• Sulfur

questions.question: Which among the following is not a type of solar eclipse?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Penumbral**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• An eclipse happens when the moon while orbiting the Earth, comes in between the sun and the Earth, due to which the moon blocks the sun’s light from reaching the Earth, causing an eclipse of the sun or a solar eclipse.
 
• There are three types of eclipses.
 
• A total solar eclipse happens when the sun, moon and Earth are in a direct line.
 
• The dark silhouette of the Moon completely covers the intensely bright light of the Sun. Only the much fainter solar corona is visible during a total eclipse which is known as a Totality.
 
• A partial solar eclipse happens when the shadow of the moon appears on a small part of the sun.
 
• Annular solar eclipse, which happens when the moon is farthest from the Earth, which is why it seems smaller.
 
• In this type of eclipse, the moon does not block the sun completely, but looks like a “dark disk on top of a larger sun-coloured disk” forming a “ring of fire”.

questions.question: The Big Dipper is an asterism formed by the seven brightest stars in the constellation:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ursa Major**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Big Dipper is an asterism made up of the seven brightest stars** in the constellation Ursa Major: 
 
• **The Big Dipper is a well-known pattern of stars that's part of the Ursa Major constellation.**
 
• It's always visible because it's circumpolar, meaning it's in the same direction as the North Star.
 
• The Big Dipper is a useful navigational tool because it points to the North Star, which is a celestial pivot point.
 
• To find the North Star, you can extend an imaginary line through the front two stars of the Big Dipper, Merak and Dubhe. 
 
• The Big Dipper is also known by other names, including:
 
 
• The Plough, Charles's Wain, Septentriones, and The Wagon. 
 
 
 
• The Big Dipper is a prominent asterism in the Ursa Major constellation, which is significant in many cultures.
 
• In Native American traditions, the stars of Ursa Major are thought to mark the changing seasons and guide spirits

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Leo Major
 
 
• Likely refers to Leo, a constellation in the night sky, sometimes called "Leo the Lion."
 
• Leo Major may be an informal way of distinguishing Leo from the smaller constellation Leo Minor.
 
• Leo is one of the 12 zodiac constellations and is visible primarily during the spring in the Northern Hemisphere.
 
 
 
• Cassiopeia
 
 
• Cassiopeia is a prominent constellation in the northern sky, named after the mythical queen of Ethiopia in Greek mythology.
 
• It is easily recognizable by its distinctive W or M shape, formed by five bright stars.
 
• Cassiopeia is visible year-round in the Northern Hemisphere and is often used to locate other celestial objects.
 
 
 
• Orion
 
 
• Orion, also known as "The Hunter," is one of the most recognizable and famous constellations.
 
• It features prominent stars like Betelgeuse and Rigel, as well as the Orion Belt, formed by three aligned stars (Alnitak, Alnilam, and Mintaka).
 
• Orion is best visible during winter in the Northern Hemisphere and has deep mythological and cultural significance.

questions.question: The Earth has been divided into many time zones. How many degrees does each time zone covers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15 degrees**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Each time zone covers 15 degrees of longitude.**
 
• There are 24 time zones in the world, so the Earth is divided into **360/24 = 15 degrees of longitude per time zone.**
 
 
• **24 degrees is the total number of degrees in a circle.**
 
• **20 degrees is not a common number of degrees for a time zone,.**
 
• **10 degrees is to Indian Standard Time o small to be a useful division of the Earth.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• India uses a** single time zone, Indian Standard Time (IST), which is UTC+5:30.**
 
• This means that IST is **5 and a half hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5a5cbce71d0e4d1726e061cd2ede0925e355cb9ed59f55f449c338f43e1dfe14.png]

questions.question: Ursa Major is a/an:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**constellation**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ursa Major** is a constellation, which is a group of stars forming a recognizable pattern traditionally named after its apparent form or identified with a mythological figure.
 
• It is one of the most famous constellations in the night sky and is also known as the Great Bear.
 
• Ursa Major contains the asterism known as the Big Dipper, which is one of the most easily recognizable patterns in the sky.
 
• The Big Dipper's "pointer" stars can be used to find the North Star (Polaris), making it an important constellation for navigation.
 
• It is visible throughout the year in most of the northern hemisphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The name "Ursa Major" is Latin for "Greater Bear," and its mythology can be traced back to several ancient cultures.
 
• In Greek mythology, Ursa Major is associated with the nymph Callisto, who was transformed into a bear and placed in the sky by Zeus.
 
• Ursa Major has been recognized and represented in various ways by different cultures, including Native American, Hindu, and Chinese traditions.
 
• The constellation is part of the family of constellations that includes Ursa Minor, Draco, and Boötes.
 
• Stars in Ursa Major are relatively close to Earth, and some of them are part of the Ursa Major Moving Group, a cluster of stars that share a common motion through space. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8ae7387496fcf04f3e95e26df75ff259177cb048128322ee2dcf411aaf8138f7.png]
